clue.text: Football team that makes us sort of cross

definitions.meaning: a Glasgow football club, founded by Irish immigrants
a ringed cross of the type carved in Ireland and Scotland

explanation.surface: A football club that makes its supporters rather angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry', but it is the noun: a Celtic cross is a stone cross with a ring round the crossing. Celtic is a famous Glasgow football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The Glasgow club bears this name, and the ringed stone cross of early Irish Christianity is named after the same people.

clue.text: Sassenach disturbed his glen

indicators.note: the letters of his glen are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A Scot is annoyed that an Englishman has upset his valley.
explanation.walkthrough: Sassenach is the Scots word for an English person, so the definition sits comfortably beside a Scottish glen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassenach is a Scottish, often scornful, term for someone from south of the border, i.e. a native of England.

clue.text: Precious odd parts of their hi-fi equipment

parts.note: precious in the sense of affectedly dainty means twee

indicators.note: the first, third and fifth letters of their are taken

explanation.surface: Something precious about the odd components of a couple's stereo system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precious' looks like valuable, but here it means affectedly quaint: twee.
explanation.definitionFit: A small loudspeaker that handles the high treble notes is part of a hi-fi set-up.

clue.text: E.g. Prince Albert's music group

definitions.meaning: Albert was husband of Queen Victoria, the spouse of a reigning monarch
a small ensemble of musicians, especially of early music

explanation.surface: Prince Albert's own band of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': Prince Albert is an example of the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The spouse of a ruling monarch has this title, and an early-music ensemble of viols or recorders bears the same name.

clue.text: Inscription on English swine's new harp

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of harp are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Words carved on an English pig's newly bought harp.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto or quotation written on a building, statue or at the start of a book is an inscription of this kind.

clue.text: Governor's arguments for and against rise of American left

definitions.note: the 's is read as 'is', so the definition is the noun governor

parts.note: pro is an argument in favour, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: in a down clue, a rise turns the word American's abbreviation upwards

explanation.surface: A governor weighs the pros and cons of the rise of the American left.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'rise of' reads upwards, so the American abbreviation turns round. 'and' is only a link between the two kinds of argument.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome the governor of a province held this office, and the word is used for colonial governors too.

clue.text: Foolishly use northern garage lacking a lubricating device

indicators.note: foolishly suggests the letters are used in a silly, jumbled order
lacking means a letter a is dropped from garage

explanation.surface: A garage up north is being misused, short of a tool for oiling machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes one A from GARAGE to leave GRAGE; with USE and N, 'Foolishly' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-pumped tool that forces grease into machine bearings is a device for lubricating.

clue.text: Inconsistencies in stories upset a girl at first

indicators.note: at first puts the overturned piece before the stories
in a down clue, upset turns the pair a and the girl's name upside down

explanation.surface: Inconsistent stories upset a young woman from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns A + MONA into ANOMA, and 'at first' places it ahead of LIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregularities or departures from what is expected are deviations of this kind.

clue.text: Called in so-called park to get a shrub

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: Hyde Park in London is so called, giving the name Hyde
called on the telephone means rang

explanation.surface: Someone telephones about a so-called park to get a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so-called park' means the name of a park: Hyde Park, the big royal park in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering garden bush with big round heads of blue or pink blooms is a familiar shrub.

clue.text: Architectural feature producing expression of wonder

parts.note: O is an exclamation of surprise
gee is an American exclamation of amazement

explanation.surface: A piece of architecture that makes people exclaim in awe.
explanation.walkthrough: The one phrase gives both exclamations, 'O, gee!' in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: An S-shaped moulding or pointed arch with a double curve is an architectural feature.

clue.text: Small number detaining an assistant for a very short time

indicators.note: detaining means holding the word an inside the other piece

parts.note: No. is a short form of number
a second is an assistant, as in a boxing or duel

explanation.surface: A minor figure holds up a helper only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: AN is held within NO, the abbreviation of number, giving NANO; then SECOND, a boxer's or dueller's helper.
explanation.definitionFit: A billionth of a second is an extremely brief interval.

clue.text: Some yob is troubling diners here

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lout is bothering the customers eating in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A small informal restaurant is a place where people eat out.

clue.text: Exotic dish male American had in Japanese port

indicators.note: had in means the American abbreviation goes inside the port

parts.note: Osaka is a major port city in Japan

explanation.surface: An American man ate a foreign meal in a Japanese harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek baked meal of minced lamb and aubergine was once exotic fare to British diners.

clue.text: Daily having links with island's good causes

parts.note: a daily is a British cleaning woman who comes every day, also called a char
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady has connections with an island's charitable work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper, but it is the old British word for a cleaning woman, a char.
explanation.definitionFit: Organisations that raise money for worthy aims are good causes.

clue.text: One who arrests criminals on board

parts.note: a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A police officer arrests lawbreakers on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship; in a down clue 'on' simply puts CONS above TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer is someone who takes people into custody.

clue.text: In which soldiers, for example, are properly dressed

definitions.text: In which soldiers, for example, are properly dressed

parts.words: In which soldiers, for example, are properly dressed
parts.note: dressing ranks means lining soldiers up straight, not putting on uniform

explanation.surface: Troops turned out smartly in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed' suggests clothing, but on parade to dress means to straighten the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers dressing their ranks are put into a straight line, the state of being arranged in a row.

clue.text: Impropriety of trendy spirit embracing form of art

indicators.note: embracing means the art style sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: Deco, as in Art Deco, is a style of art

explanation.surface: Bad behaviour with a fashionable drink and an art style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' looks as if the spirit alone holds the art form, but the fashionable word and the spirit together close round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unseemly or improper behaviour is a lack of propriety.

clue.text: Brusque statement of case?

definitions.meaning: a medical case, a person in hospital, might say 'I am a patient'

explanation.surface: A curt summary of a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' suggests law, but it is a hospital patient announcing themselves: I'M PATIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being curt and short-tempered goes with lacking patience.

clue.text: Like the current rate for working

definitions.meaning: the current price is the ... rate
a machine that is ... is working

explanation.surface: What a typical rate of pay is for a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The prevailing price is called the going rate, and a machine running smoothly is said to be up and going.

clue.text: Fellow goes back across road for aquatic plant

indicators.note: across means the reversed name stretches over the road
goes back means the fellow's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's main north road, with the 1 written as I

explanation.surface: A man walks back over the road to fetch a water plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes back' turns DAN into NAD, which spans AI. The A1 is Britain's longest road, its 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides the water nymph, the name is given to a genus of submerged freshwater plants.

clue.text: Woman reportedly swimming in sea in part of Pacific

indicators.note: reportedly means the woman's name is heard, not spelt
swimming suggests the letters of in and sea move about

explanation.surface: A woman is said to be swimming in the sea in the South Seas.
explanation.walkthrough: POLLY said aloud gives POLY; 'swimming' rearranges IN SEA into NESIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The large group of islands in the central and southern Pacific is a region of that ocean.

clue.text: The lower classes, in return, submitted

indicators.note: in places the lower classes inside the return

parts.note: a yield is a return on investment
D and E are the lowest grades in the British social classification

explanation.surface: The working classes gave way in exchange for something.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain grades social class A, B, C1, C2, D and E, so the lowest classes are D and E together.
explanation.definitionFit: To give in or surrender is to submit.

clue.text: Blow up, achieving positive result?

parts.note: in photography a blow-up from a negative gives a positive print, and a bigger result is a positive gain

explanation.surface: An explosion with a good outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow up' suggests an explosion, but it is a photographic print made larger.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a photograph is to make it bigger.

clue.text: Cold person supplying composer with precious stones

parts.note: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: An unfriendly man gives a musician some gems.
explanation.walkthrough: ICE is slang for diamonds; BERG is the composer Alban Berg.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone chilly and unemotional is called a frosty character by analogy with floating ice.

clue.text: Resolution given final backing by a business community

indicators.note: backing means the word for final runs in reverse

parts.note: net means final, as in the net result
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: A decision backed at last by a group of businesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns NET into TEN; the City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Determination or firmness of purpose is resolution.

clue.text: Girl's name I'm inclined to say out loud

indicators.note: to say out loud means the phrase is spoken, giving its sound

explanation.surface: A girl's name I feel like saying aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm inclined' looks like 'I'd like', but it means tilting: I lean.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common Irish female first name.

clue.text: Half asleep, tumbled out of bed early? Not quite yet

indicators.note: tumbled means the letters fall about into a new order
not quite means the last letter of yet is left off

explanation.surface: Drowsy someone tumbled out of bed early before quite ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the T of YET to leave YE; 'tumbled' rearranges BED, EARLY and YE.
explanation.definitionFit: Having dim, unfocused sight from tiredness describes someone barely awake.

clue.text: Goddess that's winged, but unable to fly

definitions.meaning: a Titaness, mother of Zeus in Greek myth
a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: A goddess with wings who still cannot get airborne.
explanation.definitionFit: The mother of the Olympian gods has this name, as does a big flightless bird of South America.

clue.text: Assess worth of landed property — about one million

indicators.note: about means the property surrounds the one and the million

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Value a country estate at about a million.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge roughly what something is worth is to value it.

clue.text: Remove mud from road over border

indicators.note: over means the abbreviation for road is turned round

explanation.surface: Clear mud from the road across the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'over' still signals turning round, here the road's two-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing silt from a river or harbour bed is scooping it out.
